AUTHOR: Yu
TITLE: IMM-DeepSort: An Adaptive Multi-Model Kalman Framework for Robust Multi-Fish Tracking in Underwater Environments
REGION: Coastal waters of the East China Sea, China
SPECIES: 19 marine fish species (e.g., Neopomacentrus violascens, Stephanolepis cirrhifer)
DATA: Own/partner underwater video monitoring system footage, East China Sea; frames annotated in YOLO format; 5 test video sequences + 1 additional turbid sequence
V_EV: Sec. 3.3: 'we conduct additional experiments on a newly collected video sequence characterized by high turbidity and frequent occlusion events.'
D2: 80/10/10 stratified random (images) for detector; tracking on five video sequences
D_EV: Sec. 2.5.1: 'the dataset was partitioned using stratified random sampling into three subsets: training (80%), validation (10%), and testing (10%).'
R_EV: Sec. 2.5.1: dataset 'sourced from underwater video monitoring systems deployed in the coastal waters of the East China Sea' (single source; cross-domain evaluation left to future work)
C_EV: Sec. 2.5.3: 'detection confidence threshold (0.25), NMS IoU threshold (0.45)'; Sec. 3.1: 'the number of ID Switches dropped significantly (from 32 to 16)'
E_EV: Table 3/4: only MOT metrics, e.g. 'IMM-DeepSORT achieved a MOTA improvement from 49.0 to 62.2'
ARCH: YOLOv8n detector + DeepSORT with IMM Kalman filter (CV+CA motion models)
METR: Precision, recall, mAP@0.5, mAP@0.5:0.95, AP-small; MOTA, MOTP, IDF1, FP, FN, IDS, FPS
NOTE: Headline results are tracking metrics on five video sequences; relation of these sequences to the detector's random image split is not stated (possible leakage). Confidence threshold 0.25 is a default shared across trackers. C5 coded because ID switches and FP counts are measured and the method explicitly targets ID-switch reduction; verifier should confirm whether tracking IDS reporting qualifies (if not, C_ALL = N). Extra 'newly collected' high-turbidity sequence shown only qualitatively (Fig. 9) and provenance relative to training data unclear -> R1 = N (lower-information choice). Habitat type not described (ENV NR).
